canvas.$description: Default background for portfolio pages and full-screen views.

primary.$description: Full-strength ink: headings, lead sentences, and the active state of any control.

lead.$description: Ink one step down: body paragraphs after the lead, and the active item in a guide or chip set.

secondary.$description: Supporting ink: descriptions, metadata values, navigation at rest, captions. One step below lead, so a page reads title, then lead, then everything that supports it.

tertiary.$description: Quiet ink: eyebrows, labels, inactive guide items, and footnotes. The lowest tier that still passes AA on the canvas.

quiet.$description: Decorative ink only: bullets, quote marks, and hairline glyphs. Fails AA for text at small sizes, so never set words in it.

onPrimary.$description: Dark ink used on the light primary action color.

card.$description: Raised surface used by cards that sit above the canvas.

popover.$description: Raised surface used by transient popovers and menus.

secondary.$description: Quiet secondary surface used for supporting regions.

muted.$description: Subdued surface used for intentionally low-emphasis regions.

accent.$description: Visible accent surface used for selected and highlighted states.

wash.$description: A faint wash of ink over whatever is behind it: the fill of a chip, a selected scene, a small badge. Used sparingly, because the portfolio's surfaces are outline-only by intent: a card, a media well, or a panel is a hairline on the canvas with nothing inside it.

washStrong.$description: The wash one step up, for a chip that is selected or a panel that has to separate from the well it sits in.

primary.$description: Primary action color used for the strongest controls.

destructive.$description: Destructive action color used for irreversible operations.

default.$description: Full-strength boundary for controls and structural separation.

hairline.$description: The everyday rule: card edges, table rules, and specimen frames.

faint.$description: A barely-there rule for dividing rows inside an already bounded surface.

controlQuiet.$description: The quietest control edge: a tag at rest, a supporting border on an item the fill already marks as selected.

control.$description: The everyday control edge, and the border that arrives on hover over an edge that is transparent at rest.

controlStrong.$description: A control that has to hold its own outline: a swatch frame, a segmented button.

controlSelected.$description: The selected item in a control set. The strongest border in the system, and the only one that should read as a state rather than a rule.

ring.$description: Focus ring for controls on the canvas: two pixels, no offset.

ringStrong.$description: Focus ring over media and filled surfaces, where the standard ring would sink.

selectedWork.$description: Collection accent used for Selected Work markers.

workshop.$description: Collection accent used for Workshop markers.

positive.$description: Positive status role for success, strengths, and confirmations.

faint.$description: A veil that dims what is behind it without hiding it: a resting media overlay.

DEFAULT.$description: The everyday scrim: enough to carry type over an image or a page behind a sheet.

strong.$description: A scrim that all but closes the page behind it, for a bar or overlay that owns the view.

content.$description: Maximum width for the portfolio's primary content regions.

page.$description: Maximum width for wide page and case-study layouts.

reading.$description: Maximum width for comfortable long-form reading.

touchTarget.$description: Minimum interactive target size used across navigation controls.

reference.$description: Maximum width of the design-system reference column.

narrow.$description: Characters per line for a statement or a short lead: hero copy, table notes, and single-clause captions.

body.$description: Characters per line for running prose. The default reading measure.

wide.$description: Characters per line for reference and documentation prose, where a slightly longer line keeps tables and copy aligned.
